readmeExcerpt:
# Antigravity + Gemini CLI OAuth Plugin for Opencode







Enable Opencode to authenticate against **Antigravity** (Google's IDE) via OAuth so you can use Antigravity rate limits and access models like `gemini-3.1-pro` and `claude-opus-4-6-thinking` with your Google credentials.

Unofficial plugin. Google may restrict accounts using third-party clients.

## Setup

Requires OpenCode **2.1.2+** and Node.js **20+**.

Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-antigravity-auth@2.1.1"]
}
```

Then run:

```sh
opencode auth login google
```

Choose **Google OAuth (Antigravity)**. Existing accounts are reused.

To use a local checkout, run `npm ci && npm run build` and replace the package name above with the checkout's absolute path.

## Use

```sh
opencode models
opencode run --model=google/antigravity-gemini-3.8-flash-high "Hello"
opencode run --model=google/antigravity-claude-opus-4-6-thinking#max "Hello"
```

Models are discovered from your enabled accounts and cached for an hour. Availability depends on your Google plan. Select an `antigravity-*` model for Google OAuth. Native Google API-key models are hidden while Antigravity OAuth is selected and return when you switch to an API-key connection.

Inside OpenCode, open **`/antigravity`** (or **`/ag`**) to:

- See logged-in accounts and the current selection.
- Check Antigravity and Gemini CLI quotas and reset times.
- Add, select, enable, disable, re-authenticate, or delete an account.
- Refresh the model list.

Accounts are stored in `~/.config/opencode/antigravity-accounts.json`. Back up this file before moving machines; it contains credentials. Disabling an account excludes it from rotation and routine quota checks.

## Development

```sh
npm ci
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
OPENCODE_BIN=/path/to/opencode npm run test:e2e:v2
```

The runtime test uses synthetic credentials. Authenticated model and menu checks require a logged-in Google account.

[V2 migration and verification](docs/OPENCODE-V2.md) · [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

OpenCode 1.18.29+ remains supported through the legacy entrypoint; its account menu opens from `opencode auth login`.

Update your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-antigravity-auth@2.1.1"]
```

If stuck on an old version, clear the cache:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/node_modules ~/.cache/opencode/bun.lock
```

releases.name: v1.6.5-beta.0 (Beta)
releases.body:
## Beta Release v1.6.5-beta.0

⚠️ **This is a beta release for testing. Use at your own risk.**

Base version: `1.6.5`

Compare changes: https://github.com/NoeFabris/opencode-antigravity-auth/compare/v1.6.0...v1.6.5-beta.0

- feat(auth): add Gemini CLI OAuth flow for Code Assist provisioning (610bbcc)
- fix: pause after single account verification before returning to menu (d85bac3)

### Install Beta

Update your `opencode.json`:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-antigravity-auth@1.6.5-beta.0"]
}
```

Or use the beta tag (always latest beta):

```json
{
  "plugin": ["opencode-antigravity-auth@beta"]
}
```

Clear cache if stuck on old version:

```bash
rm -rf ~/.cache/opencode/node_modules ~/.cache/opencode/bun.lock
```

releases.name: v1.6.0
releases.body:
## v1.6.0

This release contains PR #497 (merged to `main`) and focuses on request-path stability for Claude/Gemini, logging clarity, and schema/docs/test alignment.

### Fixed Issues
- **#397** - Gemini tool-call payload handling now enforces valid `thought_signature` behavior for `functionCall` parts, preventing `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` in mixed/parallel call turns.
- **#454** - Request sanitization now removes empty/invalid `contents.parts` entries and invalid `systemInstruction.parts` before forwarding.
- **#444** - Response transform fallback now uses cloned responses and preserves recovery signaling, eliminating `Body already used` failures.

### Improvements
- **#368 (tackled)** - Claude thinking/signature handling now replaces foreign signatures with sentinels and tightens thinking-order classification to reduce false-positive recovery triggers.
- **Related: #453** - `x-goog-user-project` is now stripped across Antigravity and Gemini CLI request styles, reducing project/license conflict paths.

### Changed
- `debug` now controls file logging only; `debug_tui` independently controls TUI panel logging.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A secure authentication module built for OpenCode that utilizes Antigravity technology to manage sessions.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenCode Antigravity Auth is a specialized identity and access management module designed specifically for the OpenCode ecosystem. It replaces traditional session tokens with 'Antigravity' zero-knowledge proofs, ensuring that authentication states can be verified without exposing underlying user credentials. The system provides a seamless drop-in replacement for standard OAuth flows while hardening the authentication perimeter against session hijacking and replay attacks. It includes built-in rate limiting, distributed session revocation, and native support for biometrics via WebAuthn, all orchestrated through a high-performance Rust backend.
keyFeatures: Zero-Knowledge Sessions: Authenticates users using cryptographic proofs rather than transmitting plain-text tokens or passwords.
WebAuthn Native Integration: Supports hardware security keys and biometric authentication (FaceID, TouchID) out of the box.
Distributed Revocation Engine: Instantly invalidates compromised sessions across all edge nodes globally without database bottlenecks.
Drop-in OAuth Replacement: Provides compatible API endpoints allowing existing applications to migrate without major rewrites.
Hardened Rate Limiting: Prevents brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks with sliding-window request throttling.
Rust Core Backend: Ensures memory safety and high throughput during computationally expensive cryptographic operations.

useCases.title: Enterprise identity migration
useCases.description: Upgrade legacy systems to zero-knowledge authentication without rewriting entire frontend applications.

useCases.title: High-security portals
useCases.description: Financial and healthcare platforms can utilize the module to enforce strict WebAuthn requirements and prevent session theft.

useCases.title: Edge authentication
useCases.description: Distributed applications can verify user sessions locally at the edge using decentralized proofs instead of central databases.

useCases.title: Automated bot defense
useCases.description: Operations can leverage the built-in rate limiting to automatically drop credential-stuffing traffic before it hits application logic.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Security engineers and backend developers building applications within the OpenCode ecosystem who require robust, zero-knowledge authentication mechanisms. It requires a Node.js runtime and knowledge of integrating custom authentication modules.
